name: Fourth Crusade (departure)
summary: The Fourth Crusade, intended for Egypt, is diverted by Venetian commercial interests and internal politics to attack Constantinople. Crusaders sack the city for three days (1204), looting the greatest collection of Greek and Roman art in the world. The Latin Empire of Constantinople replaces Byzantine rule; Greek successor states survive at Nicaea, Trebizond, and Epirus. The Orthodox-Catholic schism becomes irreparable.

_quarry.structural_significance: Permanently fractures Byzantine power; the wealth looted enriches Venice and other Italian cities; Nicaean Empire recaptures Constantinople in 1261 but the empire never recovers its pre-1204 strength
